> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67b491dbb44b5a564f15b8a800a079b827b61dbd` — the merge of head `061c8f78eb6c96f25fd723272bbb8f529b22308d` into base `18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67b491dbb44b5a564f15b8a800a079b827b61dbd && git checkout 67b491dbb44b5a564f15b8a800a079b827b61dbd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 061c8f78eb6c96f25fd723272bbb8f529b22308d && git checkout -B drift-repro 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 && git merge --no-ff 061c8f78eb6c96f25fd723272bbb8f529b22308d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `061c8f78eb6c96f25fd723272bbb8f529b22308d`
Local-runs: none
Independence: INDEPENDENT AGENT

Inputs read: card #23245 (body and all 4 comments: triage `6144928416`, claim `6158013575`, `os-dev-report` `6159157870`, the seat's ACCEPT `6159189302`), PR #23363 (body, 3-file list, the net diff against `main`, its one bot comment `6159144660`), and the check-runs on the head. The dev report and the ACCEPT note were weighed as claims and checked against the diff and a read-only `main` checkout; nothing was built, run or re-run. Public text stays at function level.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Active gate, session read rejects: served before, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` now.** RIGHT. This is the card's acceptance and #13906 decision 2 option B as the card cites it; REST's `computeExecCtx` and the dispatcher plugin's `readGatedSessionUser` already answer the same window with the same brand (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError('auth_gate', err)`), read on `main`.
2. **Active gate, the session API cannot be obtained or the header bag cannot be normalised: served before, `503` now** (the dev's `open_questions` arm). RIGHT, option A. The in-package sibling `readGatedSessionUser` (`dispatcher-plugin.ts`, the #23190 seam reviewed at contract tier per the card) wraps exactly these three steps in one `try` that throws the `auth_gate` brand; this diff is byte-for-byte that shape. REST's "anonymous" answer for this window is an artefact of where those steps sit in `computeExecCtx` (the identity half, above its gate block), not a ruling that an active gate admits when the read could not be started. Option B would keep a fail-open arm on an active gate, which is the shape the ruling closes. Judged inside the ruling, not a new decision.
3. **Active gate, provider mounts no session API: admitted, unchanged.** RIGHT. It returns `null` before any read, as the sibling does ("no session to hold"); the early return sits inside the new `try` but throws nothing.
4. **Active gate, no header bag on the request: admitted, unchanged.** RIGHT. No credential, no session; same early return.
5. **Inactive gate, no `auth` service, allow-listed path, or a probe that throws: admitted with no read, unchanged.** RIGHT. The outer net still returns `null` for every non-branded fault (`rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` re-raises the brand alone, the shape core prescribes); CASE 2 measures "no read" as a session-read count rather than asserting it.
6. **Active gate, read resolves with no posture (no session, un-held user): admitted, unchanged.** RIGHT. Two CASE 3 pins, through `dispatch()` and on the wire.
7. **Active gate, read carries a posture: the gate's `403` with its code, unchanged.** RIGHT. Positive control in both blocks, so a green "served" cannot mean the gate never ran.
8. **Rendering.** RIGHT, and it is structural: on `main` the call sits at `dispatch()` line 2746 and `dispatch()`'s own `try` opens at line 2796, so the branded error leaves `dispatch()` unhandled and the transport's existing `errorResponseBase` (which reads `err.status` first) answers 503. The identity step (line 698) and the membership gate (line 1590) already take this exit. No second rendering added. All four symbols the diff uses (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable`, `evaluateAuthGate`, `inProcessSessionReadInput`) are already imported on `main` (lines 4, 12, 15, 17), so the diff's unchanged import list is sound.
9. **Public surface: none moves.** RIGHT. `enforceAuthGate` is private; no export, type, schema, option or config field changes; `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` is an existing ADR-0112 code and 503 its existing mapping (core's own docblock), so the wire vocabulary is unchanged.
10. **Untouched pins.** RIGHT as claimed, verified on `main`: five runtime test files wire `isAuthGateActive`; none drives a rejecting read through an active gate at this seam expecting admission (the only matching text is the two prose lines in `http-dispatcher.root-auth-gate.test.ts`). The declared-endpoint pin (`endpoint-policy.auth-gate.pin.test.ts`) expects 503 already.
11. **Pin and negative control.** RIGHT. Nine cases, both through `dispatch()` and through the real dispatcher plugin on a recording server; the negative control (one shot, recorded in the PR body: the restored `catch { return null }` reds exactly the two outage cases, 2 failed / 7 passed, direction predicted before the run) is the card's spelling. The outage assertion checks brand, `code`, `status` and `object`, and the wire body parses under `BaseResponseSchema` and `ApiErrorSchema`.
12. **Scope.** RIGHT. Three files, all inside the claim `6158013575`: `enforceAuthGate`'s body and header only in `http-dispatcher.ts`, one new pin, one changeset. `auth-gate.ts` (#23335's file), REST's seam and every other dispatcher seam untouched. Nothing judged wrong.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-14T02:05Z, latest run per name: 24 success, 8 skipped, 7 in progress (`Check Changeset`, `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6), 0 failure. Named, not waited for: the landing is the owning seat's after green, per the ACCEPT note.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23245-dispatcher-auth-gate-outage.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` `minor`, title `fix(runtime)!:`, the launch-window BREAKING line. RIGHT. `check-changeset-no-major` records the convention: during the launch window a breaking change ships as `minor` and `major` is refused. Matches triage `6144928416` and the lane precedent the card names.
- `Clause-②:` line. RIGHT and consistent: PR body line 2 reads `no (narrowing: ...)`, the changeset reads `no (narrowing) ...`; both parse to arm `narrowing` under `readClause2Line`'s exact pattern (the look-ahead rejects only an alphanumeric or a pipe after the arm word), and `no` with `(narrowing)` is BREAKING per AGENTS.md. The facts fit: an outage window that was served is now refused, and no accept set widens.
- ADR-0087 disposition. RIGHT. Exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category in the gate's closed list. The body carries no FROM to TO rewrite (its closing paragraph is operator retry guidance, not a consumer code prescription), and no authorable key, export, option or config field is removed or renamed, so the category's precondition holds on the text.
- `skip-changeset`: not applicable; a released package publishes. RIGHT.
- `Check Changeset` was in progress at reading time; its conclusion is CI's, named above.

- Dev flag, comment drift in `http-dispatcher.root-auth-gate.test.ts` (header near line 44, control comment near line 110, read on `main`): confirmed prose only, no assertion reads it; carrier is the next PR touching that file, as the report says. Not escalated.
- Dev flag, #23335 coupling on `auth-gate.ts`: files disjoint, `evaluateAuthGate`'s contract unchanged by this diff; the later lander merges `main`. Not escalated.
- Dev flag, PR #23346 (`dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`): the head is a merge of `main` `228357ab6` carrying it; that file is not on the rendering path read above. Not escalated.
- Docs Drift Check (`6159144660`, advisory): four hand-written pages name `HttpDispatcher` by symbol; none documents this gate's outage answer, and the one release-owned page is read-only by rule. No docs edit owed by this narrowing. Not escalated.
- Report `deviations` (five, procedural: the bare-`--` re-run, the fixture-commit fetch, the full build for dist-reading gates, the `main` merge before opening, the AGENTS.md footer form): none touches the diff. Not escalated.
